Focus and Keyboard Controls

MelonUI sends input to the focused control first. If the control does not handle a key, it is passed to its parents and then to the window shortcuts.

Default Keyboard Controls

  • Tab / Shift+Tab: Moves forward or backward through eligible controls. TabIndex orders siblings, followed by insertion order; traversal through containers is depth first.
  • Alt+Arrows: Moves focus using the displayed positions of the controls.
  • Alt+Backtick: Cycles focus. Hold Shift to reverse the direction.
  • Normal Arrows: Are handled by the focused control, such as moving a text cursor or selecting a menu item.

Hidden, disabled, detached, fully clipped and zero-content-size elements are skipped. ButtonPanel is one focus stop, while QueueContainer only exposes the current card.

Focusing an Element

Find returns null when the name is missing. It throws if the name is ambiguous or the type does not match. Use a page-scoped lookup when different pages contain elements with the same name.

Focus does not change Z order. BringToFront and SendToBack are separate operations. Focusing a nonfocusable container selects an eligible child when one is available.

Adding a Shortcut

Save should be a short method with no parameters. Normal shortcut registrations match modifiers exactly. A KeyboardControl.Wildcard predicate can choose which keys and modifiers to accept.

EnableGlobalControls controls window shortcuts, and EnableSystemFocusControls controls built-in focus navigation. Neither property disables normal text editing.

Handling Input in a Custom Control

Return true only for keys that your control handles. Calling base.TryHandleKey allows registered control-specific shortcuts to run. Unhandled keys can then continue through the normal input chain.

Focus in Popups

The top active modal keeps focus and input inside it. Background window shortcuts are suppressed, and an unhandled Escape closes the popup. Closing, hiding or disabling a modal restores an eligible previous focus target. See Popups and Dialogs for more info.
